headline: Confidence scores and public benchmarks fail to certify sequence design outcomes
label: Reliability Audits For Biological Design
summary: Predicted confidence scores and public benchmarks are being audited for whether they can certify outcomes of generated biological designs.
synthesis: The dominant thread is whether outputs of design pipelines, such as predicted confidence, benchmark performance, or selection filters, license claims about designed sequences. The conformal selection study finds that public CRISPR off-target cohorts, with 10 guides, fall far short of the roughly 20,000 needed for finite-sample certification, and it reports CIRCLE-seq grouping leakage alongside free baselines. The lanmodulin study shows that structural confidence (pTM, ipLDDT) is a poor selection filter for rare-earth binding designs and points toward function-trained models on measured Tb affinity. The protein language model audit reports a steering cliff and finds that ESMFold confidence cannot certify generate-and-screen outcomes. Silscore and TriCasRank are more constructive, offering a compact siRNA potency model and a Cas12a crRNA ranker whose benefit depends on context.
